raw.query: WITH fm AS (SELECT variate, resolution, model, MIN(wape) AS wape FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE mode = 'uni' AND model IN ('chronos', 'timesfm', 'toto') GROUP BY variate, resolution, model), classical AS (SELECT variate, resolution, MIN(wape) AS wape FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE mode = 'uni' AND model IN ('naive', 'ewma', 'holt_winters') GROUP BY variate, resolution) SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN fm.wape >= classical.wape THEN 1 END) AS failed_comparisons, COUNT(*) AS total_comparisons FROM fm JOIN classical ON fm.variate = classical.variate AND fm.resolution = classical.resolution;
raw.observed: 16 of 60 (3 models x 20 cells) comparisons fail; e.g., in ctx/1min cell, best classical (ewma) wape = 0.3827355809461447 is lower than all FMs (toto: 0.38482784156650457, timesfm: 0.3853833427978712, chronos: 0.38928496938744) and in images/1min cell, ewma wape = 0.47926549309674765 is lower than all FMs (timesfm: 0.4826379762334363, toto: 0.49102008566400124, chronos: 0.4936827245990212)
raw.claimed: Three pretrained time-series foundation models beat every tested fixed-parameter classical baseline in all twenty (resolution, signal) cells
raw.evidence: In univariate mode, the best classical baseline achieved lower WAPE than the foundation models in 16 of the 60 comparisons (3 models across 20 cells). EWMA beats all three FMs in both the ctx/1min and images/1min cells.
raw.fix: Rephrase the claim to acknowledge that classical baselines like EWMA outperform the foundation models in certain configurations, such as the 1-minute resolution cells for context (ctx) and image (images) signals, where EWMA achieves lower WAPE.
